chapter: Fourteen years with Nat Cole and the recording sessions
title: Sammy Davis Jr. compared with Sinatra and Nat Cole
summary: Collins says Davis was a mimic and dancer in an entourage show, while Sinatra and Cole were giants musically.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: And I worked with Sammy also. Sammy was great but in a different way. I didn't -- you know, well Sammy has--
Well, Sammy is more of a performer. He's more of what shall -- well, he's not the musician. You understand, he's --

Well, you know, okay, if you want to call it that, you know. You know, he dabbles in -- you know, he'll get on the drums and do a few things, and you'll get the bongo and you know, they sound like Jack Costanza because that's who he used to hang around with all the time. And when Jack was with us they had to look up and there was Sammy. But Nat is -- had a different approach to it because Nat was primarily a piano player, and he could -- he was a good arranger, you know.
Frank was from the very beginning a singer. But Sammy was not, Sammy was a mimic, and a dancer. So I think his approach to -- his was strictly show business rather than --

you understand what I'm trying to say? Yeah. So I got a different feeling from him, and I didn't enjoy working with Sammy too much if you wanted to know the truth, because it was the entourage bit. You know, the great "I am" and you know. It wasn't the same feeling I got with -- I'm not taking anything from him as a performer, and as you and I know he's a great performer. But musically Sinatra and Nat -- well, that was ultimate.
Oh, that's right. Not was but Frank also.
